title: Fritaja with asparagus
description: Soft Istrian scrambled omelette with green asparagus and a little cheese. A spring breakfast when asparagus is at the market.

steps.text: Snap off the woody ends of the asparagus where they break naturally and cut the spears into 3 cm pieces.
steps.tip: Wild asparagus (šparoge) from the spring market is traditional. Thin green asparagus is the next best thing.

steps: Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan on medium and fry the asparagus for 5 minutes until tender and a little browned.
Beat the eggs with the salt and the grated cheese, pour them over the asparagus and turn the heat to low.

steps.text: Stir gently once or twice, then leave it to set for 3 to 4 minutes, until almost firm on top.
steps.tip: Istrian fritaja is softer than an omelette. Take it off while the top is still a little creamy.

steps: Cut into wedges and serve with bread.

title: Pura (polenta) with milk
description: Polenta cooked in milk until creamy, with a knob of butter and a sprinkle of sugar and cinnamon. A cheap, warming breakfast from grandma's kitchen.
steps: Bring the milk with a pinch of salt to a simmer in a pot, watching that it does not boil over.

steps.text: Pour in the polenta in a thin stream while whisking.
steps.tip: Pouring slowly and whisking stops lumps.

steps.text: Cook on low heat for 5 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
steps.tip: Instant polenta takes about 5 minutes. Coarse polenta needs longer and a splash more milk.

steps.text: Stir in the butter, spoon into bowls and sprinkle with the sugar and cinnamon.
steps.tip: Some like it with cold milk poured over, the way grandmothers served it.

title: Sirnica (filo cheese pie)
description: Layers of filo pastry and fresh cheese baked until crisp and golden. Cut a tray on Sunday and have breakfast or a snack for days.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C and oil a baking tin of about 25 x 35 cm.
Mix the cottage cheese, two of the eggs, the sour cream and the salt into a filling.

steps.text: Lay 2 filo sheets in the tin and brush them lightly with oil. Spread a thin layer of filling over. Repeat, 2 sheets with oil and a layer of filling, until everything is used, finishing with 2 sheets.
steps.tip: Keep the filo under a damp towel while you work, it dries out fast. Torn sheets are fine in the middle layers.

steps.text: Cut the pie into squares with a sharp knife before baking.
steps.tip: Cutting first means the crisp top does not shatter later.

steps: Beat the last egg with the milk and pour it evenly over the top, letting it run into the cuts.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until deep golden and puffed.

steps.text: Let it rest for 10 minutes. Eat it warm with yogurt or kefir.
steps.tip: It keeps 3 days in the fridge. Warm pieces in the oven to crisp them up again.

title: Proja (cornbread with cheese)
description: Moist cornbread with fresh cheese and feta, made with yogurt. Bake a tray for breakfasts and snacks through the week.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C and line a baking tin of about 20 x 30 cm with baking paper.
Whisk the eggs, yogurt and oil in a large bowl.

steps.text: Mix the polenta, flour, baking powder and salt and stir them into the wet mix until smooth.
steps.tip: The batter should be thick but pourable. Leave it 5 minutes so the cornmeal softens.

steps: Fold in the cottage cheese and the crumbled feta, leaving some lumps.

steps.text: Pour into the tin and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until golden.
steps.tip: A skewer pushed into the middle should come out clean.

steps.text: Let it cool for 10 minutes, then cut it into squares. Serve with yogurt.
steps.tip: It keeps 3 days wrapped and is lovely warmed up for breakfast.

title: Cheese pogačice
description: Small savoury scones with fresh cheese and grated hard cheese, crisp outside and soft inside. Good warm or cold, and they freeze well.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C and line a baking tray with baking paper. Grate the hard cheese.

steps.text: Mix the flour, baking powder and salt. Rub in the cold butter with your fingertips until it looks like breadcrumbs.
steps.tip: Cold butter makes flaky pogačice. Work quickly so it does not melt.

steps.text: Add the cottage cheese, most of the grated cheese, one egg and the yogurt and mix quickly into a soft dough.
steps.tip: Do not knead much: short mixing keeps them tender.

steps: Pat the dough out about 2 cm thick on a floured surface and cut out rounds with a glass.
Put them on the tray, brush them with the other egg, beaten, and sprinkle with the rest of the cheese and the sesame seeds.

steps.text: Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until risen and golden.
steps.tip: Keep them in a closed box for 3 days, or freeze them and warm them in the oven.

title: Roasted chestnuts with mandarins
description: Chestnuts roasted until the shells burst, peeled warm and eaten with mandarins. The smell of Zagreb streets in November.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220 °C. With a small sharp knife, cut a cross or a long slit into the rounded side of each chestnut, through the shell.
steps.tip: Without a cut they can burst in the oven. Hold each chestnut flat side down on a board so the knife does not slip.

steps.text: Soak the chestnuts in warm water for 10 minutes, then drain.
steps.tip: The water turns to steam inside the shell, so they come out softer and peel more easily.

steps.text: Spread them on a baking tray, cut side up, and roast for 20 to 25 minutes, until the shells open and the insides are soft.
steps.tip: Shake the tray once halfway so they roast evenly.

steps.text: Wrap them in a clean towel for 5 minutes, then peel them while still warm and eat with the mandarins.
steps.tip: The steam in the towel loosens the inner skin. Cold chestnuts are much harder to peel.

title: Bučnica (pumpkin and cheese pie)
description: Zagorje's autumn pie: filo pastry layered with grated pumpkin and fresh cheese, baked golden under sour cream.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C and oil a baking tin of about 25 x 35 cm. Peel the pumpkin, scoop out the seeds and grate it coarsely.
steps.tip: Hokkaido or butternut both work. A firm, sweet pumpkin tastes best.

steps.text: Sprinkle the pumpkin with half the salt, leave it for 10 minutes, then squeeze out the water with your hands.
steps.tip: Squeezing stops the pie going soggy.

steps: Mix the pumpkin with the cottage cheese, two of the eggs, half the sour cream and the rest of the salt.

steps.text: Lay 2 filo sheets in the tin and brush them lightly with oil. Spread a layer of filling over and repeat, finishing with 2 sheets of filo. Brush the top with oil.
steps.tip: Keep the filo under a damp towel while you work, it dries out fast.

steps: Beat the last egg with the rest of the sour cream and spread it over the top.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden and crisp.

steps.text: Let it cool for 10 minutes before cutting.
steps.tip: It keeps 3 days in the fridge. Warm it in the oven.

title: Pita od jabuka (apple pie squares)
description: Tender shortcrust filled with grated apples and cinnamon, baked in a tray and cut into squares. The apple cake of every Croatian home.

steps.text: Mix the flour, baking powder, {50 g} of the sugar and the vanilla sugar. Rub in the cold butter until crumbly, then add the eggs and knead briefly into a smooth dough. Divide it in two, wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
steps.tip: Knead only until it comes together. Short kneading keeps the pastry tender.

steps.text: Meanwhile peel and grate the apples. Mix them with the lemon juice, cinnamon and the rest of the sugar. Leave for 10 minutes, then squeeze out some of the juice.
steps.tip: Squeezing stops the bottom going soggy. Drink the juice!

steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Roll out one half of the dough between two sheets of baking paper and lay it in a tin of about 25 x 35 cm.
Sprinkle the dough with the breadcrumbs and spread the apples over it evenly.
Roll out the other half, lay it on top and prick it all over with a fork.
Bake for 40 minutes until golden.

steps.text: Let it cool completely, dust with the powdered sugar and cut into squares.
steps.tip: It keeps 4 days under a cover and tastes even better on the second day.

title: Kremšnite (custard cream slices)
description: Crisp puff pastry with a tall, wobbly vanilla custard and whipped cream, the famous cake of Samobor.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Prick both pastry sheets all over with a fork and bake them on lined trays for 15 to 20 minutes until golden and puffed.
steps.tip: Prick well, or the pastry rises into one big bubble.

steps.text: Let them cool. Trim one sheet to fit a tin of about 20 x 30 cm and lay it in the bottom. Cut the other sheet into 12 squares and keep them for the top.
steps.tip: Cutting the top now means you can slice neat pieces later without squashing the cream.

steps: Separate the eggs, putting the whites in a large, clean bowl. Whisk the yolks, sugar, vanilla sugar and cornstarch with {200 ml} of the milk until smooth.

steps.text: Bring the rest of the milk to the boil. Pour in the yolk mix while whisking and cook on low for 2 to 3 minutes, whisking all the time, until very thick.
steps.tip: Whisk into the corners of the pot so the custard does not catch and burn.

steps.text: Whisk the egg whites until stiff and fold them into the hot custard. Pour it straight over the pastry in the tin and smooth the top.
steps.tip: The hot custard lightly cooks the whites and makes the cream tall and airy.

steps.text: Let it cool, then chill it for a few hours until set.
steps.tip: It needs at least 4 hours, or overnight.

steps.text: Whip the cream and spread it over the custard. Lay the pastry squares on top, dust with the powdered sugar and cut along the squares to serve.
steps.tip: Keep kremšnite in the fridge and eat them within 2 days.

title: Paprenjaci (honey and pepper biscuits)
description: Old Croatian biscuits with honey, walnuts and a surprising touch of black pepper. Hard at first, they soften in a tin and keep for weeks.
steps: Warm the honey, sugar and butter in a pot on low heat until melted. Let it cool until just warm.

steps.text: Grind the walnuts and the cloves finely. In a bowl mix the flour, walnuts, pepper, cinnamon, cloves and baking soda.
steps.tip: The pepper is the secret: you taste a gentle warmth, not heat.

steps: Add the honey mix and the egg and knead into a firm, smooth dough. Wrap it and let it rest for 30 minutes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Roll the dough out about 5 mm thick and cut it into rectangles or shapes.
steps.tip: Traditional paprenjaci are pressed into carved wooden moulds. A fork pattern looks nice too.

steps: Bake on lined trays for 12 to 15 minutes until lightly golden at the edges.

steps.text: Let them cool and keep them in a tin.
steps.tip: They are hard at first and soften after a few days in a closed tin. They keep two weeks.

title: Čupavci (coconut chocolate squares)
description: Little squares of sponge dipped in chocolate glaze and rolled in coconut. A party favourite that keeps all week.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a tin of about 25 x 35 cm with baking paper.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs and sugar for 5 minutes until pale and thick. Whisk in the oil and {100 ml} of the milk.
steps.tip: It is thick enough when a ribbon of batter stays on top for a moment.

steps: Fold in the flour mixed with the baking powder, pour into the tin and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and springy.

steps.text: Let the sponge cool completely, then cut it into small squares.
steps.tip: A cold sponge cuts cleanly and does not crumble in the glaze.

steps: Melt the chocolate and butter with the rest of the milk in a pot on low heat, stirring until smooth. Keep it warm on the lowest heat.

steps.text: Using two forks, dip each square in the warm glaze, let it drip, then roll it in the coconut. Lay them on a tray.
steps.tip: Messy but fun. Keep the glaze runny, adding a splash of milk if it thickens.

steps.text: Leave them to set in a cool place for about an hour.
steps.tip: They keep a week in a closed box.

title: Kuglof (raisin bundt cake)
description: A light, lemony ring cake with raisins, baked in a fluted tin and dusted with sugar. For Sunday coffee and weekday breakfasts.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Butter a bundt (kuglof) tin well and dust it with a little flour.
steps.tip: Every groove needs butter, or the cake sticks.

steps: Whisk the eggs, sugar and vanilla sugar for 5 minutes until pale and fluffy.
Whisk in the oil, milk and the grated lemon zest.

steps.text: Fold in the flour mixed with the baking powder, then the raisins tossed in a spoon of flour.
steps.tip: Coating the raisins in flour stops them sinking to the bottom.

steps.text: Pour into the tin and bake for 40 to 45 minutes.
steps.tip: A skewer pushed into the cake should come out clean.

steps.text: Leave it in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn it out onto a rack. Dust with the powdered sugar when cool.
steps.tip: It keeps 5 days under a cake cover.

title: Sour cherry yogurt sponge
description: A quick yogurt sponge baked in a tray with sour cherries scattered over the top. Sweet, tart and easy.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a tin of about 25 x 35 cm with baking paper. Drain the cherries well.
Whisk the eggs, sugar and vanilla sugar for 5 minutes until pale and thick.
Whisk in the yogurt and oil, then fold in the flour mixed with the baking powder.

steps.text: Pour into the tin and scatter the cherries over the top.
steps.tip: Toss the cherries in a spoon of flour first so they do not all sink to the bottom.

steps.text: Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until golden.
steps.tip: A skewer in the middle should come out clean, apart from cherry juice.

steps.text: Let it cool, dust with the powdered sugar and cut into squares.
steps.tip: It keeps 4 days. In June, use fresh cherries.
